chef.name: Chef
chef.ability: You start knowing how many pairs of evil players there are.

rules.behavior: The role module counts each pair of neighbouring seats that register as evil around the seat ring, and declares the first-night step and the number shape; the engine supplies the seats and the registered teams. Spy and Recluse registration overrides apply.
rules.decision: Choose registrations; choose a false number if impaired.
examples: First-night information is computed from real players and seats
The Chef counts the pairs of neighbouring evil players around the ring
The Chef counts each pair of neighbouring players who register as evil
The Chef names every number up to the seat count as a possible answer
The Chef counts the team a player registers as, not the character

rules.behavior: The role module computes the unavoidable minimum and the possible maximum from who may register as each team, which the engine reports for the real alignments and every sober, healthy Spy or Recluse. A pair may register differently from the pair beside it, so every count in the range is legal; the engine requires the host's count.
rules.decision: Choose the count. The engine chooses no registration. A drunk or poisoned Chef still offers any number.
examples: The Chef offers the count for a Recluse registered per pair
The Chef needs no registration answer without a Spy or Recluse
A Chef whose count depends on a Recluse waits for the host and changes nothing
The Chef's computed count follows the host's registration and the offered range does not
A Spy beside the Demon may register as good to the Chef
A Spy and a Recluse beside the Demon widen the Chef's range together

investigator.name: Investigator
investigator.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Minion.

rules.behavior: Same prepared-answer path, with every Minion as a possible false answer; the pair is validated against the real Minion. A zero held in setup is no prepared answer for an Investigator: the step asks for setup. A prepared pair that relies on a Recluse registration that is impaired at the night step asks for setup instead of forcing a false answer.
rules.decision: Pick the Minion and two players; choose false information if impaired.
examples: Investigator learns one of two players is a particular Minion
The Investigator shows the answer prepared in setup and names every Minion as possible
The Investigator reads no fact, so its decision is the same whether or not its owner is drunk or poisoned

washerwoman.name: Washerwoman
washerwoman.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Townsfolk.

rules.behavior: The role module declares the first-night step and the one-of-two shape, says that the answer is the one prepared in setup and names every Townsfolk as a possible false answer. The engine reads the prepared pair from setup and writes the record of the step; `secretsErrors` validates the team and both players. A zero held in setup is no prepared answer for a Washerwoman, who always learns a character: the step asks for setup. A prepared pair that relies on a Spy registration that is impaired at the night step asks for setup instead of forcing a false answer.
rules.decision: Pick the true role and two players in `/secrets`; choose false information if impaired.
examples: First-night information is computed from real players and seats
A healthy Washerwoman refuses an answer that is not the prepared one
A poisoned Washerwoman's answer is a Townsfolk and two different players
The Washerwoman shows the answer prepared in setup and names every Townsfolk as possible
The Washerwoman reads no fact, so its decision is the same whether or not its owner is drunk or poisoned

clockmaker.name: Clockmaker
clockmaker.ability: You start knowing how many steps from the Demon to its nearest Minion.

rules.behavior: Computes the shortest seat distance from the Demon to the nearest Minion.
examples: The Clockmaker learns the distance from the Demon to its nearest Minion
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second

rules.behavior: The distance ends at the nearest Minion in play, alive or dead (Glossary "In play").
examples: The Clockmaker counts a Minion who is dead

rules.behavior: A drunk or poisoned Clockmaker has no ability, so the host chooses the number (States). The true distance stays a legal answer: the Storyteller is not required to give false information without a Vortox.
rules.decision: Give any number; the true one is allowed.
examples: An impaired Clockmaker may still receive the true distance

grandmother.name: Grandmother
grandmother.ability: You start knowing a good player & their character. If the Demon kills them, you die too.

rules.when: First night and on a Demon kill
rules.behavior: Stores the grandchild on night one; appends a death step when the Demon kills the grandchild.
The first-night step rejects a target whose real team is not Townsfolk or Outsider with `error.grandchild`; the grandchild is stored only after the check.
rules.decision: Pick a good Townsfolk or Outsider.
examples: The Grandmother cannot choose an evil grandchild

librarian.name: Librarian
librarian.ability: You start knowing that 1 of 2 players is a particular Outsider. (Or that zero are in play.)

rules.behavior: Same prepared-answer path, with every Outsider as a possible false answer; the module declares that its answer may be a zero (`orZero`), the only role that does. `zero` is the true answer when no Outsider is in play; an impaired Librarian may also be shown zero as false information when an Outsider is in play (States). Its record is written by the engine, and only for a role that declares it. An impaired Librarian with zero in play may give the true zero answer or a false Outsider pair. A prepared pair that relies on a Spy or Recluse registration that is impaired at the night step asks for setup instead of forcing a false answer.
rules.decision: Pick the Outsider and two players, or zero; choose the false information if impaired.
examples: A Librarian impaired with no Outsider in play may give the true zero answer
A paired impaired Librarian may be shown the zero as false information
A poisoned Librarian with a prepared zero is offered every Outsider and the zero
A Drunk shown the Librarian may have the zero prepared and is offered every Outsider with it
The Librarian shows the answer prepared in setup and names every Outsider as possible
The Librarian reads no fact, so its decision is the same whether or not its owner is drunk or poisoned

empath.name: Empath
empath.ability: Each night, you learn how many of your 2 alive neighbors are evil.

rules.behavior: The role module counts evil among the two nearest living neighbours; a dead seat is skipped, so the count follows deaths. The module declares the step and the number shape.
examples: The Empath counts the nearest living neighbours and follows their deaths
The Empath counts the evil players among the two living neighbours

rules.behavior: A Spy may register as good and a Recluse as evil; the role counts the team the engine reports, and the engine applies only a registration the host chooses and the registrant is sober and healthy.
rules.decision: Choose the registration for the query.
examples: The Empath counts the host's Spy and Recluse registration
The Empath counts the team a neighbour registers as, not the character

rules.behavior: The computed number is not the final answer; the engine asks the host and offers the answers the role names as possible: 0, 1 and 2.
examples: Every Trouble Brewing first-night information role offers allowed false information while impaired
An impaired Empath waits for the host's number and changes nothing
An impaired Empath returns the same answer: the engine asks the host
The Empath names every number of fingers as a possible answer

sailor.name: Sailor
sailor.ability: Each night, choose an alive player: either you or they are drunk until dusk. You can't die.

rules.behavior: Cannot die from any cause while sober and healthy, including an execution; only a bypassing ability (the Assassin) kills; an impaired Sailor dies and makes nobody drunk. A failed Sailor ability does not reactivate when the Sailor recovers. The target must be a registered-living player.
examples: The Sailor makes the chosen recipient drunk until dusk and supports choosing themself
A sober Sailor survives execution and only a bypassing kill lands
An impaired Sailor or Innkeeper makes nobody drunk or protected
The Sailor's choice makes one player drunk until dusk and the next choice ends it
A healthy Sailor makes the host's choice drunk until dusk
A poisoned Sailor or Innkeeper gives no effect and still ends the last choice

rules.behavior: The drunk effect is stored on the chosen recipient and expires at dusk.
rules.decision: Pick the player who becomes drunk.
examples: The Sailor makes the chosen recipient drunk until dusk and supports choosing themself
A Sailor or an Innkeeper who chooses the Goon is drunk and the ability fails

chambermaid.name: Chambermaid
chambermaid.ability: Each night, choose 2 alive players (not yourself): you learn how many woke tonight due to their ability.

rules.behavior: Counts how many of the two chosen players had a role step wake tonight; a step that is printed without a wake and a Demon blocked by the Exorcist do not count.
examples: The Chambermaid counts only characters who woke due to their ability
A Demon blocked by the Exorcist is not counted as having woken

rules.behavior: The step is not built when fewer than two other players are alive.
examples: The Chambermaid does not wake with fewer than two other living players

rules.behavior: `completeStep` rejects a dead target with `error.55` and a self target with `error.40`.
The count is not the final answer; the story stays a host answer.
examples: A Chambermaid choosing the Goon gets false information

rules.behavior: The wake requires two other players that `registersAlive` accepts, so a registered-dead Zombuul is not offered as an illegal choice.
examples: The Chambermaid does not wake without two registered-living choices

interactions.name: Mathematician
interactions.reason: The Chambermaid can detect if the Mathematician will wake tonight.

snakecharmer.name: Snake Charmer
snakecharmer.ability: Each night, choose an alive player: a chosen Demon swaps characters & alignments with you & is then poisoned.

rules.behavior: Requires a living target; swaps the chosen Demon's character and alignment with the Snake Charmer, poisons the new Snake Charmer permanently, and queues the new Demon in the Demon slot for the rest of that night.
examples: The Snake Charmer swaps characters and alignments with the chosen Demon
A Snake Charmer who becomes the Demon on the first night does not wake as it until the second
A Snake Charmer who chooses the Demon swaps characters and alignments with it and poisons it for good, and the new Demon wakes tonight
A Snake Charmer who chooses a player who is not the Demon, or who is poisoned, changes nothing, and a dead player is refused
A Philosopher with the Snake Charmer's ability who chooses the Demon becomes the Demon, and the Demon becomes a poisoned Philosopher
A healthy Snake Charmer who chooses the Demon swaps characters and alignments with it and poisons it

mathematician.name: Mathematician
mathematician.ability: Each night, you learn how many players’ abilities worked abnormally (since dawn) due to another character's ability.

rules.behavior: `abnormalCount` counts the distinct characters marked since the last Mathematician wake and clears the marks after the step, so a working from the preceding day still counts.
examples: The Storyteller marks abnormal abilities and the Mathematician counts them
The Mathematician counts an abnormal working from the preceding day
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second

rules.behavior: `recordAbnormal` stores one ABNORMAL mark per character with a required reason; the engine never infers that an ability worked abnormally. The marking is a Storyteller decision.
rules.decision: Mark each character whose ability worked abnormally because of another ability, and record why.
examples: The Storyteller marks abnormal abilities and the Mathematician counts them

rules.behavior: `recordAbnormal` rejects the Mathematician's own character with `error.mathematician-self`, because the Mathematician does not detect their own failing.

rules.when: While impaired or under a Vortox
rules.behavior: The computed count stays available, but the step requires a host number because the Mathematician is drunk, poisoned or hearing false information. Under a living Vortox the true number is not offered or accepted.
examples: The Mathematician requires a host number when impaired or under a Vortox

interactions.name: Chambermaid
interactions.reason: The Chambermaid can detect if the Mathematician will wake tonight.

interactions.name: Drunk
interactions.reason: The Mathematician learns if the Drunk’s ability yielded false info or failed to work properly.

interactions.name: Lunatic
interactions.reason: The Mathematician learns if the Lunatic attacks a different player than the real Demon attacked.

dreamer.name: Dreamer
dreamer.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself or Travellers): you learn 1 good & 1 evil character, 1 of which is correct.

rules.behavior: Creates a step; the engine rejects the Dreamer as the target and offers only a pair with the chosen player's character or a legal Spy/Recluse registration plus an opposite-kind character, any pair while impaired, and no raw-character pair under a living Vortox; the pool is every supported character, not the script, and an empty list refuses every answer; the pair is a secret host choice.
rules.decision: Choose the two characters; false pair if impaired.
examples: The Dreamer cannot choose themself
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second
A sober Dreamer offers only the target's character with an opposite-kind character
An impaired Dreamer may show any good and evil pair, a Vortox forbids the true one
The Dreamer may show a registered Spy or Recluse character, and a Vortox forbids the true one
An unknown target character offers no pair and the engine refuses a fabricated one

fortuneteller.name: Fortune Teller
fortuneteller.ability: Each night, choose 2 players: you learn if either is a Demon. There is a good player that registers as a Demon to you.

rules.behavior: The role module answers yes when either chosen player is the permanent red herring or registers as a Demon, and declares the two-player step and the yes-or-no shape; the engine supplies the red herring and the Demon registration. Self and dead targets are allowed.
rules.decision: Pick the red herring in `/secrets`; choose a false answer if impaired.
examples: Fortune Teller may choose themself and dead players
The Fortune Teller answers yes for a real Demon
The Fortune Teller hears yes for the Demon or the red herring and no otherwise
The Fortune Teller hears yes when either chosen player registers as a Demon
The Fortune Teller hears yes for the red herring
The Fortune Teller reads who registers as a Demon, not the character

flowergirl.name: Flowergirl
flowergirl.ability: Each night*, you learn if a Demon voted today.

rules.behavior: Computes whether a Demon voted in the ended day; a host answer is required when the Flowergirl is impaired, a living Vortox gives false information, or the ended day is missing.
rules.decision: Give the false answer when required.
examples: The Flowergirl and the Town Crier answer from the ended day
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second

rules.behavior: `recordVotes` stores the Demon voters at vote time; the Flowergirl reads that snapshot, so a later character change neither hides the original Demon nor adds a new one.
examples: The Flowergirl detects the Demon who voted before a character change
The Flowergirl ignores a later Demon who voted as a Townsfolk

towncrier.name: Town Crier
towncrier.ability: Each night*, you learn if a Minion nominated today.

rules.behavior: Computes whether a Minion nominated in the ended day; a host answer is required when impaired, under a living Vortox, or when the ended day is missing.
rules.decision: Give the false answer when required.
examples: The Flowergirl and the Town Crier answer from the ended day
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second

oracle.name: Oracle
oracle.ability: Each night*, you learn how many dead players are evil.

rules.behavior: Counts dead evil players from the current roster, not death events.
examples: The Oracle counts dead evil players, not death events
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second

undertaker.name: Undertaker
undertaker.ability: Each night*, you learn which character died by execution today.

rules.when: Other nights, only after an execution death
rules.behavior: The step exists only when `executionDeathForDay` finds a death; the wake is still the module's legacy step. The role module answers with the character recorded at the death and the characters the executed player may register as; the engine supplies both facts and writes the record of the step.
rules.decision: Choose the shown character; choose a Spy/Recluse registration; false information if impaired.
examples: Undertaker learns an execution death, not a night death
The Undertaker reads the execution of the day that just ended
An executed Recluse may be shown to the Undertaker as a Minion or the Demon
An executed Spy may be shown to the Undertaker as a Townsfolk or an Outsider
An executed Drunk is shown to the Undertaker as the Drunk
The Undertaker learns the character that died by execution today

innkeeper.name: Innkeeper
innkeeper.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they can't die tonight, but 1 is drunk until dusk.

rules.behavior: Adds protection for both targets tonight and a drunk effect on one until dusk; an impaired Innkeeper applies nothing and the failure does not reactivate when the Innkeeper recovers.
rules.decision: Pick two players and which one is drunk.
examples: An Innkeeper prevents the Pukka's delayed death and clears the poison
An impaired Sailor or Innkeeper makes nobody drunk or protected
The Innkeeper's two players are safe tonight, one is drunk until dusk and the next choice ends them
A healthy Innkeeper makes both players safe tonight and one drunk until dusk
A poisoned Sailor or Innkeeper gives no effect and still ends the last choice

monk.name: Monk
monk.ability: Each night*, choose a player (not yourself): they are safe from the Demon tonight.

rules.behavior: The role module resolves the choice into one `protected` effect for tonight; self is rejected by the shared target check; the effect ends at dawn and a new choice replaces the earlier one; an impaired Monk adds none.
rules.decision: Pick a player other than the Monk.
examples: Monk protection and Soldier safety stop the Imp
The Monk cannot choose themself
A new Monk choice ends the protection it gave before
A poisoned Monk protects no one and the Imp's attack kills
A healthy Monk returns one protection that ends at dawn

gambler.name: Gambler
gambler.ability: Each night*, choose a player & guess their character: if you guess wrong, you die.

rules.behavior: The role module resolves the guess into one intent; a wrong guess kills the Gambler through the shared ability-death path and a correct guess has no effect. An impaired Gambler's ability is suppressed.
rules.decision: Pick the target and the guess.
examples: The Gambler dies on a wrong guess and survives a correct guess
A wrong Gambler guess returns one fatal intent for the actor

rules.behavior: The step declares `canKill: false`; the engine resolves the Gambler's death through the shared ability path. The outcome control rejects any recorded death on this step, so the host cannot kill the guessed player.
rules.decision: None. The host records no death.

exorcist.name: Exorcist
exorcist.ability: Each night*, choose a player (different to last night): the Demon, if chosen, learns who you are then doesn't wake tonight.

rules.behavior: Skips the chosen Demon's step and names the Exorcist in the blocked step note (`noteVars.name`).
rules.decision: Pick a player; the Demon learns the Exorcist.
examples: An Exorcist skip resolves the Pukka's previous kill without a new poison
The Exorcist stops the chosen Demon's wake
An Exorcist who chooses the Shabaloth leaves it only the regurgitation, and one who chooses the Pukka resolves its waiting death

rules.behavior: The step projects `previousTarget` from `used.exorcistTarget` only when `used.exorcistTargetNight` is the immediately preceding night; `completeStep` rejects a repeat with `error.50`. A skipped night, death or role gap clears the restriction.
examples: The Exorcist cannot resolve a Pukka death scheduled for a later night
An impaired Exorcist stops nobody but the choice is recorded

gossip.name: Gossip
gossip.ability: Each day, you may make a public statement. Tonight, if it was true, a player dies.

rules.when: Other nights after a day statement
rules.behavior: A true statement queues a kill step for the next night.
rules.decision: Record whether the public statement was true.
examples: The Gossip statement schedules a night death only when it was true

savant.name: Savant
savant.ability: Each day, you may visit the Storyteller to learn 2 things in private: 1 is true & 1 is false.

rules.behavior: Records two private statements and which is true as `savantVisit`, once per day. A healthy Savant must declare exactly one true statement. A Philosopher who borrowed the Savant uses the same command.
rules.decision: Invent two game-related statements and choose the true one.
examples: A Philosopher who borrowed the Savant can visit once that day

rules.behavior: An impaired Savant may receive two true or two false statements; the command accepts any of `first`, `second`, `both` and `neither`.
rules.decision: Choose the truth pattern; the engine does not compute whether a statement is true.
examples: The Savant information stays one true and one false unless impaired

rules.behavior: Townsfolk abilities yield false information (Vortox), so only both statements false (`neither`) is accepted.
examples: A living Vortox makes both Savant statements false

rules.behavior: A real Savant and a Philosopher-borrowed Savant may each visit once on the same day; every visit is kept in `savantVisits`, and the latest is the `savant` record.
examples: A real Savant and a borrowed Savant each visit once a day

courtier.name: Courtier
courtier.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a character: they are drunk for 3 nights & 3 days.

rules.behavior: Adds drunk effects to every player with the chosen character until three nights later.
rules.decision: Pick the character; once per game.
examples: The Courtier makes the chosen character drunk for three nights and days, once per game

seamstress.name: Seamstress
seamstress.ability: Once per game, at night, choose 2 players (not yourself): you learn if they are the same alignment.

rules.behavior: Chooses two distinct players other than herself, computes whether they share an alignment, and spends the once-per-game ability only on a valid pair.
rules.decision: Pick the pair; give the false answer when required.
examples: The Seamstress learns whether two players share an alignment once per game

philosopher.name: Philosopher
philosopher.ability: Once per game, at night, choose a good character: gain that ability. If this character is in play, they are drunk.

rules.behavior: Stores the chosen good character, makes its owner drunk while the character is in play, and wakes the Philosopher with that ability on the same and later nights, including a borrowed death-triggered ability such as the Klutz's public choice. The drunk follows the character and ends when the Philosopher dies or is impaired; an impaired Philosopher spends the ability and gains nothing; declining does not spend it; a borrowed character counts as in play for the Pit-Hag check (r2421 How to Run token swap).
rules.decision: Pick the good character; give the borrowed ability's information under the normal information rules.
examples: The Philosopher gains the chosen ability and drunks its owner
A Philosopher who borrowed the Klutz still makes the public choice after dying
A Pit-Hag cannot create a character the Philosopher borrowed
A Philosopher who gains an information ability wakes for it in its slot, at once for a first-night ability on a later night, and from the next night when gained on the first

rules.behavior: A borrowed Juggler records guesses on their first day with the ability; a dead Philosopher who borrowed the Klutz records the public choice through the Klutz command. The holder is resolved through `hasAbility`, not the printed role alone.
rules.decision: Pick the good character; use the borrowed ability's normal command.
examples: A Philosopher who borrowed the Juggler guesses on their first day with it
A borrowed day ability acts and a Drunk's shown one does not

professor.name: Professor
professor.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a dead player: if they are a Townsfolk, they are resurrected.

rules.behavior: A living target is rejected with `error.professor-dead-only` before the once-per-game is spent; a dead target is resolved through the outcome controls. The Professor's and the Shabaloth's steps are the only night steps that bring a player back: any other step refuses a resurrection with `error.51`, and commands recorded before `tb-bmr-snv-2026-11-17.3` keep the resurrections they marked.
examples: The Professor resurrects a dead Townsfolk only

rules.behavior: The code checks the Townsfolk team and the outcome controls reject another team.
examples: The Professor resurrects only a dead Townsfolk

rules.behavior: The used flag is set, the step is not built again, and an impaired Professor does not resurrect.
examples: The Professor ability is once per game

artist.name: Artist
artist.ability: Once per game, during the day, privately ask the Storyteller any yes/no question.

rules.behavior: Records the private question and answer as `artistQuestion`: the question is free text, the answer is `yes`, `no` or `unknown`, and the ability is spent once per game. A Philosopher who borrowed the Artist uses the same command. The engine never interprets the question or computes the answer.
rules.decision: Take the Artist aside, answer honestly, and choose the answer. A drunk or poisoned Artist or a living Vortox still receives a host answer.
examples: A Philosopher who borrowed the Artist can ask the private question

slayer.name: Slayer
slayer.ability: Once per game, during the day, publicly choose a player: if they are the Demon, they die.

rules.behavior: `useSlayer` spends the ability while impaired; a Demon hit is a death, not an execution.
rules.decision: Pick the target; choose whether a Recluse registers as Demon.
examples: A poisoned Slayer spends the ability without killing
A sober Slayer kills a Recluse registered as the Demon

juggler.name: Juggler
juggler.ability: On your 1st day, publicly guess up to 5 players' characters. That night, you learn how many you got correct.

rules.behavior: The first-day guesses are recorded through the `jugglerGuess` command (0–5, repeats allowed, zero allowed); the night step exists even with zero guesses and answers with the number of matching characters, never a constant.
rules.decision: Give the false number when impaired or under a living Vortox.
examples: The Juggler may guess zero times and still learns zero

rules.behavior: The CORRECT count is stored when the guesses are recorded on the guessing day; a later character change does not change the answer. Legacy saves without a stored count fall back to the current characters.
rules.decision: Give the false number when impaired or under a living Vortox.
examples: The Juggler's answer counts the guesses from the guessing day

soldier.name: Soldier
soldier.ability: You are safe from the Demon.

rules.behavior: `soldierSafe` blocks Demon attacks while sober and healthy.
examples: Monk protection and Soldier safety stop the Imp

minstrel.name: Minstrel
minstrel.ability: When a Minion dies by execution, all other players (except Travellers) are drunk until dusk tomorrow.

rules.behavior: Makes every other player, including the executed Minion and already-dead players, drunk until dusk tomorrow; only the Minstrel is excluded.
examples: A Minion execution makes everyone except the Minstrel drunk

ravenkeeper.name: Ravenkeeper
ravenkeeper.ability: If you die at night, you are woken to choose a player: you learn their character.

rules.behavior: A conditional step is appended only if the Ravenkeeper died tonight (`appendConditionalSteps`). The role module answers with the chosen player's character and the characters that player may register as; the engine supplies both facts and writes the record of the step.
rules.decision: Choose the target and the character; false information if impaired.
examples: Ravenkeeper wakes after a night death and learns a character
The Ravenkeeper may choose any player, the Demon and its own seat included
A Recluse may be shown to the Ravenkeeper as a Minion or the Demon, alive or dead
A Spy may be shown to the Ravenkeeper as a Townsfolk or an Outsider
The Ravenkeeper learns the chosen player's character
The Ravenkeeper names every character the chosen player may register as

sage.name: Sage
sage.ability: If the Demon kills you, you learn that it is 1 of 2 players.

rules.behavior: Appends a conditional information step only after a Demon kill; the death records the attacking Demon and the engine offers only pairs with that killer while sober, any pair while impaired, and no killer pair under a living Vortox, so a later character or holder change does not move the pair; a dead second player is legal; the pair is a secret host choice and changes no game state.
examples: The Sage's death-triggered wake keeps its official slot
A sober Sage offers only pairs with the Demon that killed them
An impaired Sage may show the Demon, and a Vortox forbids it
The Sage shows the Demon who killed them after the Barber moves the Demon character

interactions.name: Recluse
interactions.reason: The Recluse might register as the Demon to the Sage.

tealady.name: Tea Lady
tealady.ability: If both your alive neighbors are good, they can't die.

rules.behavior: Protects the nearest registered-alive neighbours while both are good, so a registered-dead Zombuul is skipped; an impaired Tea Lady protects nobody.
examples: A sober Tea Lady protects a Pukka victim from the delayed death
A registered-dead Zombuul is not a Tea Lady neighbour but still counts as alive

mayor.name: Mayor
mayor.ability: If only 3 players live & no execution occurs, your team wins. If you die at night, another player might die instead.

rules.when: Night attack and end of day
rules.behavior: A lethal attack on a sober Mayor asks for a redirect, and a redirected attack is not a self-kill; an impaired Mayor has no ability; a redirect to a dead, Soldier or Monk-protected player kills nobody; at end of day, three living and no execution event win for good; a corpse execution also blocks that win.
rules.decision: Let the Mayor die, choose the replacement, or choose none.
examples: Saint loses on execution and Mayor wins at three alive without execution
A corpse execution counts as an execution event and prevents the Mayor win
A Mayor redirect onto the Imp is not the Imp's self-kill
An Imp attack on a working Mayor waits for the host's redirect and changes nothing
A redirected Imp attack kills the host's choice and journals the redirect before the attack line
The host may let the Mayor die: the answer is journaled and the death is not a redirect

fool.name: Fool
fool.ability: The 1st time you die, you don't.

rules.behavior: `bmrCannotDie` prevents the first death; the Tea Lady and Innkeeper protections resolve first, so the ability is spent only when the Fool was the reason; the Assassin bypasses it.
examples: The Assassin kills through the Fool's protection
The Fool is not spent when Tea Lady or Innkeeper protection prevents the death

virgin.name: Virgin
virgin.ability: The 1st time you are nominated, if the nominator is a Townsfolk, they are executed immediately.

rules.behavior: The first nomination spends the ability; a Townsfolk nominator is executed at once; a Drunk nominator does not trigger; the table control records and spends the first nomination even after a day execution.
rules.decision: Choose a Spy registration; decide whether an impaired Virgin triggers.
examples: Virgin executes only the first eligible Townsfolk nominator
The Virgin's first nomination is recorded after a day execution
A sober Spy registered as a Townsfolk triggers the Virgin

pacifist.name: Pacifist
pacifist.ability: Executed good players might not die.

rules.behavior: The execution `survives` flag is accepted only for a good target while a living, unimpaired Pacifist is in play and the execution is the day decision; any other use is rejected with `error.57`; a survival writes a secret host-choice line with the spared player and keeps the execution line's `prevented` consequence.
rules.decision: Decide whether the executed good player survives.
examples: The Pacifist survival flag is legal only for a good target with a sober Pacifist
SurvivalProjection follows the engine's Pacifist condition

butler.name: Butler
butler.ability: Each night, choose a player (not yourself): tomorrow, you may only vote if they are voting too.

rules.behavior: The role module resolves the choice into the master record on the Butler's seat and one `butler` effect that covers the next day's votes and ends at the next dusk; self is rejected by the shared target check; an impaired Butler's choice is kept as a record that never applies. An illegal vote is counted with a private host warning.
examples: An illegal Butler vote is counted and only warned about privately
An impaired Butler's choice is recorded with an effect that never applies
A choice the Butler made while impaired does not bind them once they are healthy
The Butler cannot choose themself

goon.name: Goon
goon.ability: Each night, the 1st player to choose you with their ability is drunk until dusk. You become their alignment.

rules.behavior: The first chooser to target the Goon is drunk until dusk and the Goon takes that chooser's alignment; a drunk or poisoned Goon grants nothing; the Lunatic and the Grandmother do not trigger it; an Assassin's kill still lands and still turns the Goon evil; a Moonchild's stored choice still kills.
rules.decision: Track the first chooser and the alignment change.
examples: The Goon drinks its first chooser until dusk and takes their alignment
A Pukka poisoned by its own poison can choose a sober Goon: it is drunk until dusk and the Goon turns evil
A permanent effect on its own source resolves beside that source's own poison
A permanent effect holds while its source is already poisoned, in either visiting order

interactions.name: Pit-Hag
interactions.reason: If the Pit-Hag turns an evil player into the Goon, they can't turn good due to their own ability.

lunatic.name: Lunatic
lunatic.ability: You think you are a Demon, but you are not. The Demon knows who you are & who you choose at night.

rules.behavior: Stores the shown Demon mask; a missing, non-Demon or out-of-script mask is rejected; the mask cannot be a bluff. Shows the host's separate good-character bluffs, using the Demon list when that choice is missing or empty. Stores the chosen target and reports it to the Demon in the step note.
rules.decision: Show the false Demon and bluffs; tell the real Demon the choice.
examples: The Lunatic's target is reported to the real Demon
The Lunatic first-night information uses its own bluffs and preserves the legacy fallback

interactions.name: Mathematician
interactions.reason: The Mathematician learns if the Lunatic attacks a different player than the real Demon attacked.

drunk.name: Drunk
drunk.ability: You do not know you are the Drunk. You think you are a Townsfolk character, but you are not.

rules.behavior: `effectiveRoleId` returns `shownRoleId`, so the shown role wakes; `isImpaired` is always true; the mask cannot leak into bluffs or the public view.
rules.decision: Pick the shown Townsfolk role and the false information.
examples: The Drunk and Lunatic masks never become bluffs or public information

interactions.name: Mathematician
interactions.reason: The Mathematician learns if the Drunk’s ability yielded false info or failed to work properly.

tinker.name: Tinker
tinker.ability: You might die at any time.

rules.behavior: `tinkerDeath` records a real ability death for a sober Tinker with `cause: "ability"` and `bmr: "tinker"`; an impaired Tinker cannot die this way. On the Tinker's night step the host marks the death on the outcome: only the Tinker dies there, and a drunk or poisoned Tinker's death is refused with `error.59`, as by day; commands recorded before `tb-bmr-snv-2026-11-17.2` keep the deaths they marked.
examples: A sober Tinker dies from an ability death during the day and the night
A protected Tinker does not die from their ability

recluse.name: Recluse
recluse.ability: You might register as evil & as a Minion or Demon, even if dead.

rules.behavior: Registration overrides feed Chef and Fortune Teller queries while the Recluse is sober and healthy; an impaired Recluse does not register, and a registration recorded for it is rejected.
rules.decision: Choose a registration for each query.
examples: Spy and Recluse registrations are explicit host choices
A drunk or poisoned Spy or Recluse registration never applies to an ability

rules.behavior: The lookup does not check `alive`; a Recluse registered as `evil` is not a Demon, while `minion` and `demon` registrations answer their own queries; impairment gates every override.
examples: A Recluse registers as evil, a Minion or a Demon and a Spy as good, a Townsfolk or an Outsider even when dead

interactions.name: Sage
interactions.reason: The Recluse might register as the Demon to the Sage.

sweetheart.name: Sweetheart
sweetheart.ability: When you die, 1 player is drunk from now on.

rules.behavior: Appends a conditional step and adds a permanent drunk effect to the chosen player that starts at the death, not at the Sweetheart's night slot.
examples: The Sweetheart makes the chosen player permanently drunk
The Sweetheart drunk starts at the death, not at the Sweetheart night slot

rules.behavior: The drunk is created only when the Sweetheart was sober and healthy at the death; a death-time poison that later expires still suppresses it.
rules.decision: Choose the drunk player; none when impaired at death.
examples: A Sweetheart poisoned at death makes nobody drunk even after recovering

klutz.name: Klutz
klutz.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player: if they are evil, your team loses.

rules.behavior: The public choice is recorded at the death through the `recordKlutzChoice` command; an evil living target makes the Klutz's team lose immediately, a target who died before the choice is refused so the host names another living player, and an impaired Klutz loses nothing.
examples: The Klutz loses the game when the public choice is evil
The Klutz public choice resolves the game as soon as the Klutz learns of the death

rules.behavior: The ability's success reads the death record's impairment, not the effect graph at the later choice; a Klutz poisoned at death loses nothing even after recovering.
examples: A Klutz poisoned at death cannot lose even after recovering

moonchild.name: Moonchild
moonchild.ability: When you learn that you died, publicly choose 1 alive player. Tonight, if it was a good player, they die.

rules.behavior: Stores the day choice and its choice-time alignment and rejects a dead target; the resolution uses the stored alignment and the Moonchild's sober/healthy state at night (Moonchild; Pukka:95), so a Goon that turns evil later still dies if it was good when chosen, a choice made while impaired still kills when the Moonchild is sober at night, and a sober choice does not kill when the Moonchild is impaired at night.
rules.decision: Pick a living player after the death.
examples: The Moonchild kills the chosen good player on the next night
The Moonchild kills a Goon that was good when chosen
A Moonchild sober at night kills the chosen good player even when poisoned at the choice
A Moonchild poisoned at night does not kill a sober choice
A living Moonchild does not wake, and a resolved one does not wake again
A dead borrowed Moonchild resolves the choice under the Philosopher's name

rules.behavior: The step kills a good target on the next night and records the resolution.
examples: The Moonchild does not kill an evil target

rules.behavior: A regurgitated Moonchild regains the choice: resurrection clears the stored target, its alignment and the resolved flag. On the next death the Moonchild chooses again.
rules.decision: Pick a living player after the second death.
examples: A regurgitated Moonchild chooses again on the next death

saint.name: Saint
saint.ability: If you die by execution, your team loses.

rules.behavior: `checkWin` reads `death.impaired` and scopes the loss to an execution death on the current day, so a cleared winner cannot re-fire.
examples: Saint loses on execution and Mayor wins at three alive without execution
The Saint loss is scoped to the day of the execution

rules.behavior: `death.impaired` is recorded and suppresses the loss.
examples: A poisoned Saint executed by the town does not lose the game for good

barber.name: Barber
barber.ability: If you died today or tonight, the Demon may choose 2 players (not another Demon) to swap characters.

rules.behavior: Appends a conditional step; swaps the two chosen characters without changing alignments, allows the choosing Demon to swap itself and rejects a swap between two Demons; with several living Demons the Storyteller chooses which one acts. The Evil Twin win follows the good twin by player and alignment, not the character's new holder.
examples: The Barber swap exchanges two characters after the Barber dies
A Barber swap grants the start-knowing ability to the new holder
A second living Demon may make the Barber swap

rules.behavior: The swap requires a death recorded while the player held the Barber. A player who dies and then becomes the Barber gets no swap.
examples: A player who died and then became the Barber enables no swap

rules.behavior: The death record's impairment gates the ability: a Barber who dies drunk or poisoned gets no swap, even after recovering.
examples: A Barber who died drunk enables no swap

rules.behavior: A Philosopher who borrowed the Barber and dies as the Philosopher gets the swap; the death record matches the current character and the borrowed ability is checked separately.
examples: A Philosopher who borrowed the Barber gets the swap after dying

mutant.name: Mutant
mutant.ability: If you are “mad” about being an Outsider, you might be executed.

rules.behavior: Stores a standing madness token for every living Mutant that requires being mad about an Outsider; the day card lists it, and `endDay` is blocked until the Storyteller records a reasoned decision. The token follows the character holder and ends with its life.
rules.decision: Judge whether the player was mad; apply `madnessPenalty` with `execute` or `none` and a reason. A `none` review may be upgraded to `execute` that day.
examples: The Mutant is mad about being an Outsider while in play
The Mutant madness follows the character holder
Ending the day is blocked until active madness has a Storyteller review
The living Mutant needs a new madness review each day
Each overlapping madness condition receives its own review

godfather.name: Godfather
godfather.ability: You start knowing which Outsiders are in play. If 1 died today, choose a player tonight: they die. [-1 or +1 Outsider]

rules.behavior: Shifts the Outsider count by ±1 and rejects impossible choices.
examples: The Godfather +/-1 Outsider setting is applied and impossible choices are reported

rules.behavior: The step carries the living Outsider list; an impaired Godfather still previews the true list, and the false list is a Storyteller statement at the table with no separate host control.
rules.decision: Show the computed Outsider list; when impaired, may show any Outsider characters.
examples: The Godfather learns the Outsiders in play on the first night

rules.behavior: The step exists after an Outsider died today; the outcome controls record the kill.
examples: The Godfather kills only after an Outsider died today

poisoner.name: Poisoner
poisoner.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned tonight and tomorrow day.

rules.behavior: The role module resolves the choice into one `poison` effect with source, target, start and expiry; it ends at the next dusk, when a new choice replaces it, when the source loses the ability, when the source dies, or when the source becomes the Demon. An impaired Poisoner adds none.
examples: Poison lasts the night and the next day, then expires
A Poisoner who becomes the Imp ends the poison it sourced
A new Poisoner choice ends the poison it sourced before and leaves another source's poison
A healthy Poisoner returns one poison for tonight and tomorrow day

devilsadvocate.name: Devil's Advocate
devilsadvocate.ability: Each night, choose a living player (different to last night): if executed tomorrow, they don't die.

rules.behavior: Adds an execution-protection effect for the next day; an impaired Devil's Advocate records the choice but creates no protection, and the failure does not reactivate on recovery.
examples: The Devil's Advocate prevents tomorrow's execution death
An impaired Devil's Advocate protects nobody after recovery
The Devil's Advocate's choice gets tomorrow's execution protection, and the next choice ends it
A poisoned Devil's Advocate protects nobody but the choice is recorded and the last one ends
The survives-execution dated effect is stored as the Devil's Advocate's protection for the next day

rules.behavior: The step projects `previousTarget` from `used.devilsadvocateTarget` only when `used.devilsadvocateTargetNight` is the immediately preceding night; `completeStep` rejects a repeat with `error.50` and a dead or registered-dead target with `error.55`. A skipped night, death or role gap clears the restriction; a legacy record without a night is unknown.
examples: The Devil's Advocate cannot choose the same target on consecutive nights
An impaired Devil's Advocate protects nobody but the choice is recorded

rules.behavior: The execution-protection check runs before the Zombuul's first-death replacement, so a protected Zombuul executed today stays alive and keeps its life token and its own first death.
examples: A Devil's Advocate-protected Zombuul keeps its first death

spy.name: Spy
spy.ability: Each night, you see the Grimoire. You might register as good & as a Townsfolk or Outsider, even if dead.

rules.behavior: The role module declares the step of every night with the grimoire shape and says that its ability shows the Grimoire; the engine records that it was shown and stores no answer in its place. Registration overrides answer good, Townsfolk and Outsider queries, including for a dead Spy, only while the Spy is sober and healthy.
rules.decision: Show the grimoire; choose registrations; show a false grimoire if impaired.
examples: A Recluse registers as evil, a Minion or a Demon and a Spy as good, a Townsfolk or an Outsider even when dead
A drunk or poisoned Spy or Recluse registration never applies to an ability
The Spy sees the Grimoire
The Spy reads no fact, so its decision is the same whether or not its owner is drunk or poisoned

witch.name: Witch
witch.ability: Each night, choose a player: if they nominate tomorrow, they die. If just 3 players live, you lose this ability.

rules.behavior: Stores a curse on the target; the next nomination kills the nominator but keeps the nomination; a sober, healthy Witch places the curse; the curse is inactive while the Witch is impaired or dead without Vigormortis retention, resumes on recovery, and does not kill at three or fewer living.
examples: The Witch curse kills the nominator but keeps the nomination
A placed Witch curse does not kill after the Witch dies or is impaired
The Witch loses a placed curse only when exactly three players live

cerenovus.name: Cerenovus
cerenovus.ability: Each night, choose a player & a good character: they are “mad” they are this character tomorrow, or might be executed.

rules.behavior: Creates the step, stores the chosen player and good character as a madness token that lasts until the next night, and creates none when the Cerenovus is impaired or the choice is incomplete. The token is a persistent effect: it stops while the Cerenovus is drunk, poisoned or dead and resumes when the source is healthy again; a Vigormortis-retained Cerenovus keeps it (States, Glossary, Vigormortis). The day card lists the target, and `endDay` is blocked until the Storyteller records a reasoned decision.
rules.decision: Choose the player and the good character; judge madness, then apply `madnessPenalty` with `execute` or `none` and a reason. A `none` review may be upgraded to `execute` that day.
examples: The Cerenovus marks the chosen player mad for the next day and night
A poisoned Cerenovus suspends the madness and it resumes when healthy
A dead Cerenovus ends the madness
An expired or removed madness token stops applying
The Storyteller executes a player who failed to be mad
The madness penalty only accepts the legal Storyteller options

pithag.name: Pit-Hag
pithag.ability: Each night*, choose a player & a character they become (if not in play). If a Demon is made, deaths tonight are arbitrary.

rules.behavior: Changes the target's character but not their alignment, filters the offered characters, records the legal "nothing happens" outcome when the chosen character is already in play, gives a created Demon no normal Demon turn (its deaths are ability deaths), offers the arbitrary deaths only after a Demon is created, rejects a marked death on a step that allows none, and lets the normal win check resolve the new roles.
rules.decision: Pick the target and one absent character; resolve arbitrary Demon deaths only after creating a Demon.
examples: The Pit-Hag replaces a character atomically
A Pit-Hag-created Demon does not take the Demon turn and its deaths are not Demon attacks
A Pit-Hag death marked under the earlier ruleset keeps its death
A player the Pit-Hag makes the Town Crier wakes in its slot and one made the Clockmaker wakes at once
A character created mid-game gains its start-knowing information that night

interactions.name: Goon
interactions.reason: If the Pit-Hag turns an evil player into the Goon, they can't turn good due to their own ability.

assassin.name: Assassin
assassin.ability: Once per game, at night*, choose a player: they die, even if for some reason they could not.

rules.behavior: Kills through the Fool's, Sailor's, Tea Lady's, Innkeeper's and Devil's Advocate's protection; the Goon still dies and turns evil.
examples: The Assassin kills through the Fool's protection
The Assassin kills through the Tea Lady's protection
The Assassin kills the Goon and the Goon still turns evil

rules.behavior: Declining keeps the ability; a chosen target spends it even while impaired, and then no later step is built. An unknown target and a duplicate completion change nothing. Professor restores a used once-per-game ability on resurrection.
examples: An Assassin who declines keeps the ability for a later night
An Assassin never wakes again after a kill
An impaired Assassin spends the ability without killing
A resurrected Assassin regains the once-per-game ability

eviltwin.name: Evil Twin
eviltwin.ability: You & an opposing player know each other. If the good player is executed, evil wins. Good can't win if you both live.

rules.behavior: Requires a good twin. The pair is the two stored players and the win reads the good twin's real alignment. The ability holder is the current `eviltwin` character holder (either pair member) and must be alive and unimpaired unless a living, unimpaired Vigormortis retains the ability; the execution resolves before its death, so the two twins may swap. A dead Evil Twin without such retention, or one out of play, stops the win and the both-live block; a Pit-Hag-created Evil Twin builds its pair so the win and the block stay active; imported legacy saves backfill the pair.
examples: Executing the good Evil Twin wins the game for evil
A dead Evil Twin cannot win on the good twin's execution
An Evil Twin killed by the Vigormortis still wins on the good twin's execution
A Pit-Hag-created Evil Twin keeps the twin win and the good-win block
The Clockmaker and the Evil Twin wake on the first night only, the Dreamer and the Mathematician every night, and the Flowergirl, the Town Crier and the Oracle from the second

rules.behavior: `checkWin` returns no winner while both twins live and no Demon remains; killing the last living twin then lets good win by `demon-dead`.
examples: Good cannot win while both Evil Twins live even with no Demon
An Evil Twin that leaves play stops the twin win and the block

rules.behavior: The host correction `manualCorrection` with `kind: "twin"` validates an Evil Twin holder, a living partner and opposing real alignments, then writes the two player ids and the good twin's role; an invalid correction changes no setup field.
examples: The host can set the Evil Twin's good partner
The host can pair a good player who became the Evil Twin with an evil player
A twin correction requires an Evil Twin holder
A same-alignment partner is rejected

rules.behavior: The pair is one good and one evil player and is never inferred: a character gained mid-game leaves both player ids unset, and the night cannot end until the host records the partner with the `twin` correction. The stored ids name each side, so the execution win reads the right player.
examples: A Pit-Hag-created Evil Twin needs the host's explicit partner
A Pit-Hag-created Evil Twin starts unpaired and blocks the end of the night (P0.2)

rules.behavior: A save whose stored pair has the same alignment is repaired on import: the good side and the evil side are rebuilt from the stored players and the roster.
examples: An imported same-alignment twin pair is repaired

mastermind.name: Mastermind
mastermind.ability: If the Demon dies by execution (ending the game), play for 1 more day. If a player is then executed, their team loses.

rules.behavior: Runs the intervening night with normal eligible abilities, then one extra day; the team of the player executed on that day loses.
examples: The Mastermind extends the game by one day after a Demon execution

interactions.name: Vigormortis
interactions.reason: A Mastermind that has their ability keeps it if the Vigormortis dies.

scarletwoman.name: Scarlet Woman
scarletwoman.ability: If there are 5 or more players alive & the Demon dies, you become the Demon. (Travellers don't count.)

rules.behavior: `resolveDemonDeath` requires five registered-alive players before the death and a sober Scarlet Woman; a player other abilities see as dead (a registered-dead Zombuul) does not count. The heir becomes the Demon and does not act again that night.
rules.decision: Pick the heir when several Minions are eligible after an Imp self-kill.
examples: Scarlet Woman inherits only with five living before the Demon dies
A registered-dead player does not count toward the Scarlet Woman's five

rules.behavior: `endDay` carries the Demon-change flag into the next night and appends the `demonchange` step, so a succession during the day still wakes the new Demon with the YOU ARE token, once; a change made the night before, already woken that night, is not carried.
rules.decision: Show the new Demon the YOU ARE and Imp tokens.
examples: The new Demon is woken the night after a daytime Scarlet Woman succession
A Scarlet Woman who takes the role by day after a night self-kill is woken the next night, once
A Demon who died on an earlier day does not make a later night change wake twice

interactions.name: Fang Gu
interactions.reason: If there would be two Demons, one of which was the Scarlet Woman, the Scarlet Woman remains the Scarlet Woman.

baron.name: Baron
baron.ability: There are extra Outsiders in play. [+2 Outsiders]

rules.behavior: `compositionFor` adds two Outsiders and removes two Townsfolk.
examples: Composition table is exact and Baron shifts two Townsfolk to Outsiders

pukka.name: Pukka
pukka.ability: Each night, choose a player: they are poisoned. The previously poisoned player dies then becomes healthy.

rules.behavior: Stores a `poison` effect on the chosen player and a `pukka-death` effect that resolves at the next Pukka step; the previous victim dies and becomes healthy.
examples: The Pukka poisons immediately and kills the previous victim next night

rules.behavior: The new poison lands before the previous victim's death, so a newly poisoned protector (for example the Tea Lady) cannot save the old victim.
examples: The Pukka poisons the new target before the previous victim dies

rules.behavior: A drunk or poisoned Pukka applies no new poison and suspends the pending death; the poison resumes when the source is healthy.
examples: An Exorcist skip resolves the Pukka's previous kill without a new poison

rules.behavior: An Exorcist skip still resolves the previous victim's death; Innkeeper or Tea Lady protection prevents it and clears the poison.
rules.decision: Pick the Exorcist target; pick the Innkeeper patrons.
examples: The Pukka poisons immediately and kills the previous victim next night

rules.behavior: A dead Pukka stops poisoning and cancels the pending death.
examples: A dead Pukka stops poisoning and cancels the delayed death

rules.behavior: The Pukka poisons itself; the previous victim becomes healthy and its pending death is suspended. A healthy Pukka resolves that death immediately; when it chooses again, it dies as the previous target after the new poison.
rules.decision: Pick the Pukka as the target.
examples: The Pukka choosing itself poisons itself and suspends the previous death

rules.behavior: A later poison or drunk effect on the Pukka suspends its earlier poison and pending death. The ability resumes only after the last impairment ends; removing one impairment while another remains keeps the death suspended.
examples: The Pukka poisons the new target before the previous victim dies
A Pukka poisoned by its own poison can choose a sober Goon: it is drunk until dusk and the Goon turns evil

nodashii.name: No Dashii
nodashii.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Your 2 Townsfolk neighbors are poisoned.

rules.behavior: Poisons the nearest Townsfolk on both sides by character, including dead ones; reconciles on death, role change and source loss.
examples: The No Dashii poisons the nearest Townsfolk even when that seat is dead

rules.behavior: The poison ends when the No Dashii dies; the effect graph requires a living source for the non-permanent poison.
examples: The No Dashii poison ends when the No Dashii dies

imp.name: Imp
imp.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. If you kill yourself this way, a Minion becomes the Imp.

rules.behavior: The role module resolves the choice into an `attack` decision; `resolveAttack` applies an impaired attacker, a dead target, the Monk, the Soldier and the Mayor's redirect; a self-kill passes the role to a Minion; the new Demon's remaining step is skipped; the new Demon is woken once, that night: the wake of a named heir is queued with the choice, and the next night does not wake it again.
rules.decision: Pick the target; resolve a Mayor redirect; pick the heir.
examples: Imp self-kill passes the role and the new Demon does not act again
Monk protection stops the Imp; a poisoned Monk does not
The Soldier is safe from the Imp while sober and dies while poisoned
Mayor redirect to a dead player kills nobody and the Mayor lives
A poisoned Imp cannot kill itself and no new Demon is created
An Imp attack on a working Mayor waits for the host's redirect and changes nothing

shabaloth.name: Shabaloth
shabaloth.ability: Each night*, choose 2 players: they die. A dead player you chose last night might be regurgitated.

rules.behavior: Two kills and an optional resurrection are recorded through the outcome controls; the chosen targets are stored with their night, and the outcome may resurrect one of them only on the immediately following night. A Lunatic shown the Shabaloth attacks as it but regurgitates no one, and no other step brings a player back (`error.51`).
rules.decision: Pick two targets and the regurgitated player.
examples: The Shabaloth kills two players and can regurgitate a target from last night

po.name: Po
po.ability: Each night*, you may choose a player: they die. If your last choice was no-one, choose 3 players tonight.

rules.behavior: Chooses zero or one target; after a no-target night, exactly three targets.
examples: The Po may hit three players only after a night with no choice
The Po's choice of no one is recorded, also when it is poisoned, and a Po kept asleep keeps its last choice
The Po's choice of a player is recorded with its death, and a Po who chooses the Goon is drunk
An impaired Po's choice is recorded the same way: the next night still takes three players

zombuul.name: Zombuul
zombuul.ability: Each night*, if no-one died today, choose a player: they die. The 1st time you die, you live but register as dead.

rules.behavior: The first death is replaced and registers as dead, and a Death entry is recorded for that day so the Zombuul stays awake-free; other abilities see it as dead (Tea Lady neighbours, the Scarlet Woman's five) while the game's own alive count keeps it; the second death kills; wakes only if nobody died today.
examples: The Zombuul survives its first death but registers as dead
The Zombuul's first death is recorded and keeps it from waking that night
A registered-dead Zombuul is not a Tea Lady neighbour but still counts as alive

rules.behavior: The day path counts a registered-dead Zombuul as dead: it cannot nominate and its first vote spends the token. The execution threshold keeps the game's own living count; the interpretation stays open in #313.
examples: A registered-dead Zombuul cannot nominate and its vote spends the token

vigormortis.name: Vigormortis
vigormortis.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Minions you kill keep their ability & poison 1 Townsfolk neighbor. [-1 Outsider]

rules.behavior: Removes one Outsider and rejects the impossible choice.
examples: The Vigormortis minion keeps its ability and poisons one Townsfolk neighbour

rules.behavior: A Minion killed by the Vigormortis keeps its night step and ability (including the Evil Twin execution win) while a living, unimpaired Vigormortis exists and the dead Minion itself is sober and healthy; a drunk or poisoned dead Minion loses the retention until it is sober, and a dead or impaired Vigormortis prunes the step.
examples: The Vigormortis retention ends when the Vigormortis dies
A drunk dead Minion loses the Vigormortis retention and the neighbour poison until sober
A Vigormortis poison still waits for its dead Minion, so a cycle through that Minion is rejected

rules.behavior: Poisons one Townsfolk neighbour (the clockwise nearest by default) with a host override naming the other legal neighbour; the poison ends with the Vigormortis or when the killed Minion stops being a Minion, and it needs a real kill.
examples: The Vigormortis poison needs a real Minion kill

rules.behavior: Every Minion killed by the Vigormortis keeps its ability and creates its own poison; the engine keeps one poison effect per killed Minion.
examples: The Vigormortis retains every killed Minion and poisons for each

interactions.name: Mastermind
interactions.reason: A Mastermind that has their ability keeps it if the Vigormortis dies.

vortox.name: Vortox
vortox.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. Townsfolk abilities yield false info. Each day, if no-one is executed, evil wins.

rules.behavior: A day with no execution wins for evil.
examples: The Vortox wins when the day ends without an execution

rules.behavior: A living, unimpaired Vortox (or an impaired Townsfolk) makes every computed Townsfolk answer require a host answer, so the engine never presents the true value as final.
examples: An impaired information role demands the host's answer

fanggu.name: Fang Gu
fanggu.ability: Each night*, choose a player: they die. The 1st Outsider this kills becomes an evil Fang Gu & you die instead. [+1 Outsider]

rules.behavior: Adds one Outsider; the first Outsider killed becomes an evil Fang Gu and the old Demon dies.
examples: A first Outsider death makes the Outsider the new Fang Gu and kills the old Demon
The Outsider the Fang Gu jumps into wakes as the Fang Gu from the next night

rules.behavior: The game-scoped `fangguJumped` flag keeps the ONCE reminder for the rest of the game; a later Outsider kill is a normal death. Legacy per-player markers, resets and export/import are covered.
examples: The Fang Gu jump can happen only once per game

rules.behavior: The jump requires a living Outsider target and an actual death. An Outsider chosen while already dead is not changed and the Fang Gu does not die.
examples: A Fang Gu attack on an already dead Outsider does not jump

rules.behavior: A drunk or poisoned Demon has no ability. The outcome path rejects every recorded death from an impaired Sects and Violets Demon with `error.52`.
examples: A drunk Sects and Violets Demon kills nobody
